body.p: Attorney Docket No.: 06530-0802-03000 AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMS:
This listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application:

br.br:
1 - 20. (Cancelled)219
21. (New) A medical device, comprising:
a shaft; and
an assembly coupled to a distal end of the shaft, the assembly including a plurality of arms circumferentially spaced apart from one another about the distal end and a sensor coupled to each of the plurality of arms;
wherein the plurality of arms are configured to move relative to the distal end between a first position and a second position;
wherein, in the first position, the plurality of arms are in an undeployed configuration such that each of the plurality of arms lie substantially flush relative to the distal end, and in the second position, the plurality of arms are released to a deployed configuration such that each of the plurality of arms extends radially outwards relative to the distal end.
22. (New) The medical device of claim 21, wherein, in the first position, the sensor on each of the plurality of arms faces radially inwards towards the distal end and is in an inoperable state for emitting light and detecting a light intensity resulting from the emitted light.
23. (New) The medical device of claim 22, wherein, in the second position, the sensor on each of the plurality of arms faces radially outwards from the distal end and is in an operable state for emitting light and detecting the light intensity resulting from the emitted light.
24. (New) The medical device of claim 21, wherein the assembly includes a cuff having a distal end and a proximal end, the proximal end being configured to slidably attach over the distal end of the shaft to couple the assembly to the shaft.
25. (New) The medical device of claim 24, wherein each of the plurality of arms includes a first end and a second end that is opposite of the first end, the first end being mounted to the cuff, and the second end being movable relative to the cuff.
26. (New) The medical device of claim 25, wherein the first end of each of the plurality of arms defines a hinge such that the second end of each of the plurality of arms is configured to pivot via the hinge.
27. (New) The medical device of claim 26, wherein, in the first position, the second end of each of the plurality of arms is positioned proximal relative to the first end, and in the second position, the second end of each of the plurality of arms is positioned distal relative to the first end.
28. (New) The medical device of claim 24, wherein the cuff includes a plurality of recesses formed between the proximal end and the distal end of the cuff, and circumferentially spaced apart from one another about an exterior of the cuff; and
wherein the plurality of recesses are configured to receive the plurality of arms when in the undeployed configuration.
29. (New) The medical device of claim 21, wherein each of the plurality of arms includes a proximal side and a distal side, and each of the plurality of arms has a preset shape with a concave curvature along the distal side and a convex curvature along the proximal side.
30. (New) The medical device of claim 21, wherein the plurality of arms are biased towards at least one of the undeployed configuration and the deployed configuration.
31. (New) The medical device of claim 21, wherein the plurality of arms are configured to passively move between the first position and the second position in response to the shaft moving relative to a bodily lumen and one or more surrounding tissue surfaces of the bodily lumen contacting the plurality of arms.
32. (New) The medical device of claim 31, wherein the assembly is configured such that the plurality of arms move from the undeployed configuration to the deployed configuration in response to the shaft moving distally relative to the bodily lumen, and
from the deployed configuration to the undeployed configuration in response to the shaft moving proximally relative to the bodily lumen.
33. (New) The medical device of claim 21, further comprising an actuator configured to move the plurality of arms between the first position and the second position in response to activating the actuator.
34. (New) The medical device of claim 21, wherein the plurality of arms are configured to stabilize the shaft within a bodily lumen by engaging surrounding tissue surfaces of the bodily lumen and centralizing a field of view within the bodily lumen when in the deployed configuration.
35. (New) The medical device of claim 21, further comprising a controller communicatively coupled to the sensor on each of the plurality of arms;
wherein each sensor on the plurality of arms includes an emitter configured to emit light and a detector configured to detect light;
wherein the controller is configured to calculate separate perfusion indices corresponding to a light intensity measured by the detector over time as reflected off of bodily tissue from light originating at the emitter of the same sensor.
36. (New) A medical device, comprising:
a shaft having a distal end for deployment within a bodily lumen; and
an assembly coupled to the distal end and including two or more arms each having a sensor, the two or more arms being configured to move relative to the distal end between a first position and a second position;
wherein, the two or more arms are positioned substantially flush with the distal end in an undeployed configuration when in the first position, such that the sensor on each of the two or more arms is inoperable for emitting light and detecting light intensity;
wherein, the two or more arms are positioned distally relative to the distal end in a deployed configuration when in the second position, such that the sensor on each of the two or more arms is operable to emit light and detect a light intensity from within the bodily lumen.
37. (New) The medical device of claim 36, wherein the assembly includes a cuff having a proximal end configured to slidably attach over the distal end to couple the assembly to the shaft;
wherein each of the two or more arms includes a first end that is pivotably mounted to the cuff and a second end opposite of the first end that is movable relative to the cuff about the first end.
38. (New) The medical device of claim 37, wherein the second end of each of the two or more arms is positioned within a recess of the cuff when in the first position, and extended outside of the cuff when in the second position.
Attorney Docket No.: 06530-0802-03000 39. (New) The medical device of claim 36, further comprising a controller communicatively coupled to the sensor on each of the two or more arms, wherein the controller is configured to calculate a separate perfusion index corresponding to a light intensity measured by a detector of each sensor in response to light emitted by an emitter of the same sensor.
40. (New) A medical device, comprising:
a shaft; and
an assembly coupled to a distal end of the shaft, and including a plurality of arms that are flexibly movable relative to the distal end;
wherein, in a first position, the assembly is undeployed with the plurality of arms positioned laterally inwards towards the distal end such that a sensor on each of the plurality of arms faces inwards towards the distal end; and
wherein, in a second position, the assembly is deployed with the plurality of arms positioned laterally outwards from the distal end such that the sensor on each of the plurality of arms faces outwards away from the distal end.
